# Swap the outside parts (copy and adapt)

For a team that copies Faro’s code rather than rebuilding it from this kit: every part of the outside world Faro touches (its database, who is signed in, the time, files, where a metric’s numbers come from) sits behind one interface in `src/ports/`, with a contract test any replacement must pass. Moving Faro onto your platform is writing one adapter per part you swap, until its contract passes. Supabase is imported only by its own adapters, `src/adapters/supabase/`, and the layers lint (`npm run lint:layers`, rule 4) keeps it so.

**Today:** each part’s contract runs on Faro’s own adapters in `npm test` (`src/adapters/stores.test.ts`, `src/adapters/parts.test.ts`, `src/adapters/deps.test.ts`). The goals store’s is proven twice over: the Supabase adapter (on a stand-in for Supabase’s client, `src/adapters/supabase/testClient.ts`, over real Postgres with every migration) and a second, plain-Postgres adapter pass the same contract.

**The goals store is the demo-scale port.** `Store` loads a whole workspace and saves rows its caller wrote. That is right for a demo of 126 goals and wrong for 15,000 people: [R4](../requirements/internal/r4-scale-and-safety.md) says nothing loads a whole workspace, and [R1](../requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md) says the server enforces the rules. Writing a `Store` adapter gets Faro running on your database; it is not the shape of the internal app. Read R1, R4 and [the ports at company scale](ports-at-scale.md) before you write one.

## Entry criteria

- A copy of Faro’s repository, with `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` passing on it unchanged.
- [R1](../requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md), [R4](../requirements/internal/r4-scale-and-safety.md) and [the ports at company scale](ports-at-scale.md) read, so you know which adapters are for getting started and which ports replace them.
- For each part, a decision: keep Faro’s adapter, or write your own.

## The parts

| Part | Interface | Contract | Adapters today |

## What to build

- **An adapter per part you swap**, in its own folder under `src/adapters/` (yours, say `src/adapters/acme/`), that implements the interface and imports your platform’s client. Nothing outside that folder imports the client: add your package to the layers lint’s rule 4 as Supabase is.
- **Its contract test**: a test file that calls the part’s contract with a way to make your adapter, as `src/adapters/stores.test.ts` does for Faro’s. Use a real but disposable instance of your service where you can (Faro’s Postgres contracts run on PGlite, Postgres in WebAssembly, with every migration).
- **The wiring**: where the app picks an adapter. The browser picks its goals store in `src/main.tsx`, its markups and feedback in `src/markup/backend.ts`, who is viewing in `src/app/state.tsx`; the AI tools’ endpoint picks its `Deps` in `server/vercel.ts`.
- **Copying the Supabase adapter** (`src/adapters/supabase/goalsStore.ts`): it is the worked example of a store. Every read either succeeds or fails the load (an empty list would look like a workspace with none); a database function that isn’t there says the migrations are missing, apart from a request that failed; and every save, new workspace and deletion is one call to one database function, so one transaction.
- **The database, if you keep Postgres without Supabase:** run `src/adapters/postgres/bootstrap.sql` once (stand-ins for Supabase’s roles and its storage and auth schemas), then every migration in `supabase/migrations` in order (from 0035 Faro’s tables and functions live in their own schema, `faro`: connect with `search_path` set to `faro`, or as a role whose default it is; a migration after 0036 writes its grants out, since Supabase’s defaults don’t apply there, makes no redirect in `public`, and reaches nothing outside `faro`: `supabase/README.md`), then use `PostgresStore` (and `postgresDeps` for the AI tools’ endpoint) with node-postgres or any driver with a `query(text, params)` method. What the migrations add up to is [one file to read](../core/schema.sql), and who may do what today is [access today](access-today.md): all of it the demo’s, to replace. The database’s functions (`okr_commit` and the rest) only check that rows belong to the workspace (each row’s own, not the records it points at) and that goal and review versions haven’t moved; every other rule, the actor, the time and the change-log entry come from the caller today (`src/domain/actions` run in the browser). A company-scale rebuild moves those actions to the server (R1, R4), so read them before you build on this port: [the ports at company scale](ports-at-scale.md) sketches the route.
- **The feature modules’ records:** a goals store keeps the core’s tables by name and every module’s by what the module declares (`src/domain/records.ts`; each module’s `records.ts`, listed under `records` in its `module.json`). It iterates over the declared records: it reads each one’s table into `modules[module][key]` with the record’s `fromRow`, and writes a save’s rows with `toRow` in the same transaction as the rest (Faro’s `okr_commit` takes them by table, from an allowed list a module’s migration adds its tables to: migration 0039). A record a build doesn’t declare is neither read nor written, so a workspace keeps its rows while a module is left out. The contract runs with a small test module of its own (`CONTRACT_MODULE`), so an adapter that names a module’s tables can’t pass it.
- **Sign-in:** an `Identity` whose `current(workspaceId)` answers, asynchronously, with the person in that workspace whose email the sign-in gives (or null), and which has no `choose`: `src/adapters/signIn.ts` is the shape, and passes `identityContract`. Pass it to the app beside the store (`src/main.tsx`); nothing in the core changes. Outside the demo the app never acts as a stand-in: nobody signed in, or a sign-in that matches no one, sees none of the workspace and can save nothing: one page says they can’t open it yet, why (not signed in; no one has the email; more than one person has it; only someone marked as left or removed has it: the optional `why` on `Identity`, which `signInIdentity` answers), and offers a message to send whoever set it up and Try again (`WhoAreYou`, `src/screens/Start.tsx`). Who is signed in is asked each time a workspace opens, not on the two-minute reload, so someone removed while the app is open keeps reading until they open it again; the server’s rules stop their saves (R1). Who may change what is still the server’s to enforce ([R1](../requirements/internal/r1-sign-in-and-access.md)).
- **Numbers:** a `NumberSource` per system your metrics name as their source (a warehouse, a dashboard’s API). A metric’s `source` says which.

## What Faro keeps in the browser

Records go through the goals store; a few small things a person chose or was doing are kept in the browser instead. Behind the `Prefs` port (`src/ports/prefs.ts`, kept by `browserPrefs` in `src/adapters/local.ts`) today: what was opened lately, the Goals scope used last, and when each goal was last looked at. These files still reach the browser’s storage directly, from the layers lint’s shrinking list (`scripts/browser-storage.json`, rule 7: no new file may), with where the internal app should keep each. “Server” means it should follow the person between devices, so it moves behind `Prefs` or the goals store; “this browser” means it is about one tab or device and stays.

| File | What it keeps | In the internal app |
|---|---|---|
| `index.html` | Nothing of its own: reads the appearance keys (src/app/appearance.ts) before the first paint, so there is no flash | This browser: a copy of the person’s appearance, for the first paint |
| `src/app/appearance.ts` | Appearance: theme, accent, sidebar, motion, sound and story mode | Server: a person’s preference, on every device |
| `src/app/demoBrowser.ts` | Nothing of its own: clears the demo’s keys when the demo is reset | Not needed: the demo only |
| `src/app/drafts.ts` | Unsent check-in and form drafts | Server: a draft follows the person from laptop to phone |
| `src/app/research.ts` | A research session in progress and its notes | Not needed: Faro’s own research sessions |
| `src/app/state.tsx` | The workspace opened last | Server: a person’s preference |
| `src/app/tours.ts` | A guided tour in progress (this tab) | This browser |
| `src/data/store.ts` | The browser store itself (the demo’s records and saves) and the demo’s workspace | Server: the goals store (the browser store is the demo’s adapter) |
| `src/help/seen.ts` | The last What’s new entry the person has seen | Server: a person’s preference |
| `src/markup/backend.ts` | The markups this person sent, and, with no database, markups and their pictures (IndexedDB) | Server: the markup store and its files |
| `src/markup/feedback.ts` | Feedback triage kept in this browser when there is no database | Server: the feedback store |
| `src/screens/CheckInFlow.tsx` | The check-in queue for the week (this tab) and the step a check-in reached | Server for the step (it is part of a draft); the queue stays in this browser |
| `src/screens/DataLayout.tsx` | Each table’s columns and layout on Data | Server: a person’s preference |
| `src/screens/GoalMap.tsx` | Where goals were moved on the Map, and its only-in-trouble switch | Server: a person’s preference |
| `src/screens/GoalViews.tsx` | The Goals list’s layout | Server: a person’s preference |
| `src/screens/reviewOrder.ts` | The order of a review’s goals (this tab) | This browser |
| `src/screens/QuickCheckIn.tsx` | Nothing of its own: clears a check-in’s step once it is saved | Server, with the step (see CheckInFlow) |
| `src/telemetry/ids.ts` | The telemetry session id (this tab) | This browser |
| `src/telemetry/staleCode.ts` | That the page has already reloaded once for new code (this tab) | This browser |
| `src/ui/BackLink.tsx` | The trail of pages for Back (this tab) | This browser |
| `src/ui/Demo.tsx` | Who the demo is viewed as | Not needed: sign-in says who it is (R1) |
| `src/ui/ResearchBar.tsx` | Research tasks skipped (this tab) | Not needed: Faro’s own research sessions |
| `src/ui/Shell.tsx` | Presenting mode on or off (this tab) | This browser |
| `src/ui/Splash.tsx` | That the opening splash has been shown (this tab) | This browser |
| `src/ui/WorkspaceSwitch.tsx` | Nothing of its own: looks for unsent drafts before switching | Server, with the drafts |

79 uses in 25 files. The time is a port too: every record’s stamp comes from the `Clock` the app is given (`src/app/state.tsx`), never the browser’s own.

## Exit criteria

1. Each adapter you wrote passes its part’s contract.
2. `npm run lint:layers` passes: your platform’s client is imported only in your adapter’s folder.
3. `npm test` and the smoke evals (`npm run evals:smoke`) pass with your adapters wired in.
4. Stage 1’s drill still scores 100% (the rules don’t depend on any adapter).

## Gaps in the kit

- The plain-Postgres adapter covers the goals store; markups, feedback, files and telemetry still go to Supabase in Faro itself (telemetry sends to Supabase’s REST address, `src/telemetry/exporter.ts`).
- The goals store’s, goal lists’, Search’s and Prefs’ contracts are in this folder as data ([the port contracts](../conformance/contracts/README.md)), and the drill harness runs them on any build through a shim. The small parts’ contracts (markups, feedback, identity, the picker, the clock, files, number sources and the dependency checks) still live only in Faro’s code (`src/ports/contracts/`): a rewrite from the spec alone can read what they check here but can’t run them.
